mechanic.prompt:
Goal: apply the Builder pattern for creating Table instances by providing a concrete TableBuilder implementation and wiring Connection to return a builder.

Create a new class org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.DefaultTableBuilder that implements org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.TableBuilder with private final org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.Connection connection and private final org.apache.hadoop.hbase.TableName tableName fields, mutable fields int operationTimeout, rpcTimeout, readRpcTimeout, writeRpcTimeout and long writeBufferSize; add a package-private constructor DefaultTableBuilder(Connection connection, TableName tableName) that assigns the finals; implement each setter to set the corresponding field and return this; implement build() to delegate to the existing table-creation logic by returning connection.getTable(tableName).

Modify org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.Connection by adding a new method public org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.TableBuilder getTableBuilder(org.apache.hadoop.hbase.TableName tableName) { return new DefaultTableBuilder(this, tableName); } and change the existing public Table getTable(TableName tableName) to delegate to getTableBuilder(tableName).build(); (no other API changes).

architect.prompt: Apply the Builder pattern by refactoring HTable construction and configuration into a new TableBuilder/TableBuilderBase API—have ConnectionImplementation create and configure TableBuilder instances (drawing parameters like rpcTimeout from ConnectionConfiguration), change getTable to delegate to getTableBuilder, and refactor HTable to be constructed from the builder (retaining deprecated setters for backwards compatibility) so existing construction logic is relocated into the builder without changing external behavior.

product_owner.prompt:
Title: Construction/configuration logic embedded in HTable hinders extensibility and maintenance

Description: HTable currently owns construction and configuration state (fields, setters, and constructors), which couples creation to implementation, forces deprecated setters to remain for compatibility, and makes adding new table types or changing config brittle and error-prone. Centralizing creation/configuration into a single construction component will decouple responsibilities, allow producing different table implementations cleanly, and reduce maintenance and testing overhead.

tdd.prompt: A senior engineer has written a test that encodes the desired new builder-based API; refactor the codebase so this test passes.
